events.text: Q1 FY26 (10-Q): total revenue $1,474.2M (+18.7% y/y); GAAP income from operations $431.3M (29.3% margin); NI $335.7M; diluted EPS $1.23 (vs $1.00). Recurring/up-front mix 77%/23% (vs 82%/18% in Q1 FY25, skewed to up-front by Palladium/Protium hardware + IP timing). Backlog (RPO) $8.0B (up from $7.8B at FY25 year-end). China came back strong: $189.4M (+36% y/y, ~13% of revenue).

CDNS signed for IP on Intel's 14A node — cited by BofA as a foundry-credibility signal in the INTC double-upgrade, and a reminder that Cadence earns collateral regardless of which foundry/customer wins the node war.

Simpson's live read on the 07-27 Q2 print: "I thought it was very strong." The streak is quantified — "yet again another beat and raise from these guys. That's been about five or six quarters in a row" — which is the direct counter to JPM's 07-27 buyside survey complaint that "the magnitude of the beats has been shrinking": the frequency is unbroken even if the magnitude compressed. Record backlog and the new Intel deals "somewhat caught the eye." The standout, and a harder claim than the published note's "additive growth vector": "what really stood out for me was the agentic EDA opportunity. This does look like a DEMAND ACCELERATOR for these guys" — i.e. agents pull more volume through the existing engines rather than sitting alongside them, which is management's own rebuttal to the Kimi-K3 displacement bear stated by the sell side. Product completeness is the enabling fact: "they've got the full design flow now open as an offering." Evidence on the ground: ChipStack has 20+ customer engagements with a number now paying, and NVIDIA is named as a user. Monetisation comes from both the agentic workflow products and higher usage of the underlying EDA stack — but the timing is deliberately grounded: a small amount in 2H26, "really a 2027 story." No PT restated on the webcast (MS Overweight $400, raised from $370 the same day).
